cards.text: Hosea the prophet is bringing the LORD's words to Israel, and this message opens with an alarm: "Put the ram’s horn to your lips!" An eagle looms over the house of the LORD. Friend, when a message starts with a HORN BLAST, nobody's about to get a compliment.

cards.question: Why does God say the alarm is sounding over His people Israel?

answers.text: They lost a battle at the border

cards.text: Then Israel cries out to God, "O our God, we know You!" That's me telling a baker, "I know this recipe by HEART," while the smoke alarm goes off behind me.

cards.question: After Israel claims to know Him, God answers that Israel has held on to what is good.

cards.text: God says an enemy will pursue Israel. Then He runs down the list of what they've been doing, starting with who's in charge.

cards.question: Israel sets up kings and makes princes. What's God's problem with them?

answers.text: They did it without His approval
They taxed the people too hard

cards.question: Israel takes its own silver and gold and makes ___ for itself, to its own destruction.

cards.text: Then God calls out one idol by name, the calf of Samaria: "My anger burns against them. How long will they be incapable of innocence?" Friend, you don't ask HOW LONG about something that happened once.

cards.question: Where does God say the calf of Samaria came from?

answers.text: It was carried in from Egypt
It was a gift from Assyria

cards.question: God says the calf of Samaria will stand for many years to come.

cards.text: Then comes the big line: "For they sow the wind, and they shall reap the whirlwind." Read that one twice, friend, and I'll wait right here.

cards.question: God says Israel sows the wind and will reap the whirlwind. What's the picture?

answers.text: What they plant comes back far bigger
Their fields need more rain to grow
A storm will pass right over them

cards.text: Plant a breeze, harvest a TORNADO. And the fields give nothing: what sprouts yields no flour, and even if it did produce, foreigners would swallow it up.
"Israel is swallowed up!" Now they're out among the nations like a worthless vessel, and friend, I KNOW that feeling from years in the back of a junk drawer under the takeout menus.

cards.question: Israel goes off on its own, like a wild donkey, up to another nation. Which one?

cards.text: Then Hosea uses another name for Israel, the northern kingdom: Ephraim. And Ephraim has hired lovers, friend, like paying somebody to answer your texts.

cards.question: Ephraim hires allies among the nations, and God says those allies will keep Ephraim safe.

cards.text: Instead, God says He will round them up, and they will begin to diminish under the oppression of the king of princes.
Ephraim multiplied the altars for sin, and they became his altars for sinning. And God says He wrote out the great things of His law for them.

cards.question: God wrote out the great things of His law for Israel, and they regarded it as something ___.

cards.text: Then the sacrifices. They offer them as gifts to God, and they eat the meat.

cards.question: The LORD accepts the sacrifices Israel offers Him as gifts.
God says He will remember Israel's iniquity and punish their sins. Where does He say they will return?

cards.text: Israel has forgotten his Maker and built palaces, and Judah, the southern kingdom, has multiplied its fortified cities. That's like forgetting your own name but remembering the WiFi password.

cards.question: Israel built palaces and Judah built fortified cities. What does God say He will send upon their cities?

findings.problem: The question asks why the alarm (the ram's horn) is sounding. In Hosea 8:1, the 'because' clause gives the reason the eagle looms over the house of the LORD. The text never says it is the reason the horn is blown, so the card supplies a link the text leaves open. Asking why the eagle looms over the house of the LORD would stay with the text.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The joke shows Israel's claim as hollow: someone says they know the recipe by heart while the smoke alarm goes off. That gives away card 4, which asks whether Israel has held on to what is good (8:3). The setup rules out True before the baker has to reason it out.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Hosea 8:6's key statement that the calf 'is not God' is never told on any story card. The verse also says the calf is 'from Israel', and that isn't told either. Card 9 asks only about the craftsman and card 10 only about the calf being broken, so the baker can leave Prep without the central point of the verse.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: In Hosea 8:9, the core action of 'hired lovers' is paying for love or allies. 'Paying somebody to answer your texts' most naturally means hiring someone to reply for you, which is a different action. A stranger would say 'huh?' This needs a comparison where someone pays for affection or friendship.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: Story cards 5, 6 and 8 are bare retellings with no reaction, comparison or storyteller line. For example, card 8 is only 'Then the sacrifices. They offer them as gifts to God, and they eat the meat.' Most of stop 2's middle reads stripped down rather than in Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The question says Judah 'built fortified cities'. Hosea 8:14 says Judah 'has multiplied its fortified cities', and story card 11 uses 'multiplied' correctly.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.
